chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام.
Regarding the one struck unconscious and the drowned person, he said: “One waits for him for three days, unless he changes before that.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, said: If lote leaves, camphor, and ushnaan are not found for the deceased, he is washed with plain water. If fragrant powder and hanūt are not found for him, he is wrapped in his shrouds and buried after his washing and the prayer over him. If he has no shrouds, he is buried naked, and that is permissible due to necessity.

The basis in that is that preparing the deceased is only obligatory when one has the means and ability to do so. So whenever the means and ability cease, the obligation falls away, because Allah Most High says: “Allah does not burden a soul except to its capacity,” and He is more entitled to grant excuse in a state of necessity.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, said: If a person dies at sea and no land is found for him in which he may be buried, he is washed, given hanūt, shrouded, his shrouds are sewn upon him, he is weighted, and he is cast into the sea so that he may sink by his weight to the bottom of the water.

key_terms.الِاضْطِرَارِ: a state of necessity or compulsion
key_terms.الْمَصْعُوقِ: a person struck down unconscious or apparently lifeless
key_terms.تَجْهِيزَ الْمَيِّتِ: the preparation of the deceased for burial
key_terms.حُنِّطَ: was perfumed with burial ointment or hanūt

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings for washing and burying a deceased person when burial materials are unavailable or death occurs at sea?
ai.summary: This text sets out legal rulings for handling the deceased in difficult circumstances, such as uncertainty of death, lack of burial materials, or death at sea. It emphasizes that the rites of preparing the dead are obligatory only according to one’s ability, invoking the Qur’anic principle that Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity.
